newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL BLUE-CHIP INDEX FALLS BELOW 900-POINT BARRIER.
newsitem.headline: KL BLUE-CHIP INDEX FALLS BELOW 900-POINT BARRIER.

text.p: Malaysian's key blue-chip share index fell below the key psychological barrier at the 900-point level in mid-afternoon trading.
There was a bloody, but brief battle as the index attempted to breach 900. The size of foreign selling prevailed and the barrier was broken at 0729 GMT.
At 0735 GMT, the Composite Index was down at 899.66 points.
"It seems like foreigners want to get out of the ringgit," said a dealing manager at a local brokerage.
"Almost everybody agrees that 880 is the next support level. There is only limited support around 900," he said.
"U.S. hedge funds are continuing to get out of the ringgit instruments and that is hurting stocks," said an associate director of research at a foreign brokerage in Kuala Lumpur.
The ringgit fell to a 42-month low of 2.7300 to a dollar at around 0430 from around 2.6850 in early morning trading. At 0742 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.7410/60.
The decline followed Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's comment on Friday that Malaysia was happy with the ringgit's level.
Share prices were down across the board with little sign of recovery in mid-afternoon trading.
